free.a: Yes. Message checks, learning and family protection are free for citizens. Only companies that embed the check in their own services pay.

data.a: We check it with rules and send it to Google Gemini for AI analysis. We do not store the text itself: only a masked record and the score remain, and they are deleted after 90 days. Metadata is removed from screenshots first.

accuracy.q: How far can I trust the score?
accuracy.a: A score is a hint, not a guarantee. We always show what it is based on. If in doubt, call your bank on the number on the back of your card. You can dispute a wrong score.

scammed.q: I have already been scammed. What now?
scammed.a: Tap "I was scammed" at the top of the screen. It gives a step-by-step plan for the first hour: your bank, 102 and collecting evidence.

family.a: Yes. In Family you can agree on a safe word and, with your relative's consent, see only their risk level, never their messages.

business.q: I represent a bank or a marketplace
business.a: Businesses get an API that checks a recipient before payment. Prices are published openly on the pricing page.

callMode.title: Is someone calling you right now?
callMode.lead: Scammers keep you on the line so you have no time to think. Tap a question to see what to say.

safeWord.a: Ask for your family safe word. If they don't know it, hang up and call your relative yourself.

code.q: Are they asking for an SMS code?
code.a: It's a scammer. Banks and the government never ask for codes. Hang up.

bank.q: Do they say they're the bank or the police?
bank.a: Hang up and call back yourself: your bank on the number on your card, the police on 102.

money.q: Are they asking you to send money or take a loan?
money.a: Don't. A "safe account" or "take a loan to protect your money" are the clearest signs of fraud.
